title: Simple In-Order Fine-Grained Multithreaded Cores vs. Out-of-Order Superscalar Cores
decision: Use eight simple, single-issue, in-order 6-stage pipeline cores, with each core supporting four fine-grained multithreaded (FGMT) execution contexts (32 total threads per chip).
alternatives_or_rejected: Fewer complex out-of-order (OoO) superscalar cores with deep pipelines and speculation logic.
rationale: Commercial server workloads (databases, web servers, application servers) exhibit frequent memory stalls and low instruction-level parallelism (ILP). Out-of-order execution logic consumes massive area and power for minimal gain in commercial applications, whereas fine-grained multithreading switches threads every cycle to efficiently hide memory latency using thread-level parallelism (TLP).
outcome: Maximized commercial workload throughput per watt and per unit area within a modest ~63W power envelope.

title: Single Shared Floating-Point Unit (FPU) Across All Eight Cores
decision: Implement a single shared Floating-Point Unit (FPU) connected via the crossbar to serve all eight cores, rather than integrating FPUs within each core.
alternatives_or_rejected: Integrating a dedicated FPU inside every core or sharing FPUs between pairs of adjacent cores.
rationale: Target commercial workloads perform very few floating-point operations. Placing dedicated FPUs in each core would waste die area and leakage power that could otherwise be used for L2 cache and thread processing.
outcome: Significantly saved die area and reduced static power while meeting the sparse floating-point requirements of commercial benchmarks.

title: On-Chip Crossbar Interconnect for Core-to-L2 Cache Communication
decision: Implement an 8x4 crossbar switch providing direct, concurrent connections between the 8 cores and 4 banked L2 cache partitions.
alternatives_or_rejected: A shared bus architecture or ring network interconnect.
rationale: A shared bus would rapidly saturate under the simultaneous memory traffic generated by 32 active thread execution contexts. The crossbar provides deterministic, high-bandwidth, low-latency access to all L2 banks.
outcome: Sustained over 130 GB/s of crossbar interconnect bandwidth, keeping 32 threads fed without interconnect bottlenecks.

title: Integrated On-Chip Memory Controllers
decision: Integrate four DDR2 memory controllers directly onto the processor die.
alternatives_or_rejected: Using external off-chip memory controller logic chips.
rationale: Off-chip memory controllers add pin latency and limit memory bandwidth, which severely impacts multithreaded throughput when servicing frequent cache misses across 32 threads.
outcome: Delivered high aggregate memory bandwidth (~25 GB/s peak) and reduced latency directly to the on-chip L2 cache banks.
